name: Forchach
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny, secluded mountain village in the Lechtal – a hidden gem for those seeking peace and nature lovers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Forchach is situated at an altitude of 910 meters in the lower Lech Valley in the district of Reutte, nestled scenicly between the Lechtal and Allgäu Alps. Home to approximately 250 residents, this peaceful village ranks among the smallest and most unspoiled municipalities in Tyrol. The village displays a classic Tyrolean nucleated settlement layout, featuring sun-darkened timber farmsteads, decorative wall paintings, and blooming gardens. Set within the core of the Tiroler Lech Nature Park—Europe's last largely untouched wild river landscape—Forchach is renowned for its expansive braided gravel banks, braided channels, and light pine riparian woodlands, offering nature enthusiasts an oasis of serenity far from mass tourism.

History

Settlement in the valley dates to the High Middle Ages, with the village first documented in 1200 under the name Vorhach. Derived from Middle High German, the name signifies a pine forest, evoking the extensive pine woods blanketing the alluvial river fan. For centuries, the community subsisted on mountain agriculture and timber under the historic court jurisdiction of Ehrenberg near Reutte. In 1635, villagers erected a plague chapel dedicated to Saint Sebastian, rebuilt in 1742 into the charming baroque church with its elegant steeple. The village's signature landmark is its suspension footbridge over the wild Lech: originally constructed in 1906 by hunters and foresters as a 75-meter cable bridge, it stood for over a century as a local symbol. Following an extensive river widening and ecological restoration project by the nature park expanding the river bed to over 130 meters, a magnificent new 138-meter suspension bridge was completed in August 2020, hanging 16.7 meters above the wild river for pedestrians and cyclists.

Getting There

By automobile from Germany, Forchach is reached entirely toll- and vignette-free via motorway A7 through Füssen and Reutte along the scenic B198 Lechtal highway in approximately fifteen minutes. From Vorarlberg, route B198 runs via Warth down the valley. Rail passengers travel via the Außerfernbahn railway to Reutte in Tirol station, connected by direct hourly trains from Munich, Garmisch-Partenkirchen, and Kempten. From Reutte railway station, VVT regional bus line 110 runs frequent scheduled services stopping directly in Forchach. Public regional buses are complimentary or discounted for visitors carrying the Lechtal Aktiv Card.

Tips

Walking across the 138-meter Forchach Suspension Bridge is a breathtaking highlight, offering direct aerial views down into the braided turquoise currents and gravel islands of the wild Lech. Long-distance hikers along the renowned Lechweg trail cross the bridge on the stage between Stanzach and Weißenbach. The barrier-free bridge also welcomes cyclists touring the family-friendly Lech Cycle Path, with natural gravel beaches inviting refreshing dips in summer. Wildlife photographers and birdwatchers in the protected riparian reserve can spot endangered pioneer plant species like the German tamarisk alongside rare nesting birds such as common sandpipers. Mountain hikers can ascend the Schwarzhanskarspitze (2,227 m) in the surrounding Lechtal Alps.
metaDescription: Forchach in the Lech Valley: Naturpark Tiroler Lech, spectacular 138m suspension bridge, pristine gravel banks, Lechweg trail and traditional alpine hamlet.
